title: Guarded Staircase Scheduler for latency-led scaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a new autoscaling controller ("Guarded Staircase Scheduler") for Dedicated fleets that prioritizes latency SLOs while bounding cost and preventing oscillation. The controller will combine latency-percentile targets, throughput-derived demand signals, and a staircase (tiered step) scaling algorithm with safety fences (max step, cooldowns, burst credits, and emergency venting). This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation in the policy-orchestrator, e2e tests, and a staged rollout with telemetry and rollback hooks.
proposed_solution: 1) Composite target metric: primary = p95 latency SLA per tenant; secondary = sustained tokens/sec demand. 2) Signal fusion: compute short-window (30s) and long-window (10m) demand; use derivative and variance to detect spikes. 3) Staircase scaling algorithm: scale in discrete tiers (e.g., +10%, +25%, +50%) with exponential backoff for rapid increases and capped step sizes for decreases. 4) Safety limits: per-tenant max-step, fleet-level cost ceiling, minimum cooldown, headroom credit accounting, and surge quarantine that routes excess traffic to fallback model variants. 5) Damping & smoothing: derivative damping and Quantile-smoother to avoid reacting to transient noise. 6) Integrations: expose controls in Console for target p95, cost cap, burst allowance. 7) Metrics & alerts: alert on frequent scale flapping and when headroom credit reaches 0.
decisions: Use p95 latency as primary SLO: agreed due to product tolerance for occasional p99 spikes but strict p95 requirement
Staircase tiers chosen: 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 2x capacity to balance granularity vs churn
Cooldown semantics: min_cooldown = 120s for up-scales, min_cooldown = 300s for down-scales to prevent oscillation
Burst credits: per-tenant credit buckets that allow short-term oversubscription; credits decay linearly over 1h
Emergency venting: on consecutive failed scale attempts or control-plane errors, route lowest-priority tenants to a best-effort fallback
Cost cap enforcement: controller will reject auto-scaling beyond fleet cost ceiling and trigger ops page to request manual approval
tasks: Design doc: complete architecture and safety model (Confluence)
Simulations: implement load generator scenarios and run Monte Carlo sims to tune tier thresholds
Controller prototype: add Staircase scaling mode to policy-orchestrator service
Telemetry hooks: add headroom_credit, scale_decision_reason, scale_step, cooling_window to metrics
E2E tests: synthetic spike, sustained growth, noisy traffic, control-plane outage
Console controls: UI for tenant-level p95 target and burst credit allocation
Runbook: create ops playbook for manual intervention and rollback
Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% with a kill switch
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic spike workload, >95% of tenants maintain p95 latency below configured target after one allowed tier escalation
Scale events per tenant < 6/hour during noisy traffic tests (no flapping), unless sustained demand warrants more
Cost regression vs baseline < 5% for steady-state traffic profiles
Headroom credit accounting prevents >2x billing overcommit for tenants with depleted credits
Controller exposes decision_reason in logs and metrics for every scale action
Canary rollout completes without triggering emergency venting or manual rollback at 10% stage
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged internal fleets + integration tests (2 weeks). Stage 2: Canary on low-risk customers (1% traffic, monitor 48h). Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 10% (monitor 72h) and 50% (monitor 1 week). Stage 4: Full rollout with default conservative knobs. Each stage includes preflight checks (SLOs, cost delta, scale event rate) and an immediate kill switch to revert to previous autoscaler.
